_README: Groups S, C, D — everything the Performance panel can settle. Copy to
Six figures per configuration, deterministic, about a second each. ONE
VARIABLE PER ROW - every row names what it changed from the baseline. If
two things moved, the row is discarded, not interpreted.
S1 IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. What the Top Speed readout responds to is what
the readout IS, and the app's oldest unresolved question rides on it:
Boston's reading is that it is the projected maximum with the whole build
aimed at top speed, but it moved 140.0 -> 144.4 across the GR86
final-drive sweep, so it is not independent of the tune either. Both
cannot be true as stated. The SET of inputs it moves with settles it.
Do S3 before S2. If 0-60 barely moves between the worst and best tire,
the car is power-limited and S2's thirty minutes are not worth spending

baseline._note: the app's road tune for this car — every S row returns here before changing one thing

S0_repeatCheck._note: S0 — RUN THIS FIRST, EVERY SESSION, and fill it before any other block. Move one slider a step off its value and back, six times: three arriving from above, three from below, nothing else touched, nothing saying SIMULATING when the figure is read. The spread across these six IS this session's noise floor, and any later difference smaller than it is no result. The from-above and from-below groups must also agree; if they do not, that is path dependence and it is worse than variance. Do NOT copy a previous session's numbers in here — measured once on 2026-08-12 the spread was essentially zero, but Boston has seen the figures move by more than that elsewhere, so the floor belongs to the configuration, not to the game.
S0_repeatCheck.spreadNote: write the observed spread per figure here once the six rows are in, e.g. '0-60 0.000, top speed 0.0, 100-0 0.1 ft'

S1_topSpeedRespondsTo._note: S1 — vary ONE input, return to baseline, vary the next. Record Top Speed each time. The set that moves it defines what the number is.

S3_tractionOrPowerLimited._note: S3 — do this before S2. Big 0-60 change = traction-limited, the launch group matters. Small = power-limited, skip S2 on this car.

S2_accelerationFactors._note: S2 — one variable per row, all returning to baseline.

S4_braking._note: S4 — 5 balance points x 3 pressure points. The cleanest experiment in the catalogue: brake balance depends on nothing but wStep, and the panel measures braking directly. Tests brake-bias-per-width-step (currently 1.5% per step, no source at all).

S5_lateralGRespondsTo._note: S5 — THE SLEEPER. If lateral G moves with camber and pressure and not just compound, a whole group of lap-times-only constants becomes measurable standing still. Ten minutes to find out.

C1_disciplineSignatures._note: C1 — parts FIXED, only the tune changes, so this costs no shopping. Tarmac only: dirt and cross-country tunes on the panel just look worse because the panel is not testing them on dirt. Write the predicted ordering in `prediction` BEFORE reading.

D3_awdCentreSplit._note: D3 — AWD only. The app's neutral base moved 55 -> 60 on ForzaTune's band without ever being measured.
